renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: n50_vs_length
  title: Contiguity against assembled length
  description: |-
    Each point is one assembly: its total assembled length on the horizontal axis and its contig N50 on the vertical axis, coloured by assembler and sized by the number of contigs. It answers which assembler gives the most contiguous assembly for the length it recovers.
    How to read: points toward the upper right assemble more of the community in longer contigs. A large point low on the axis is a fragmented assembly, many small contigs, which a binner will struggle with. Compare assemblers on the same sample before choosing one.
    Note: QUAST defines no pass mark for N50 or assembled length. The vertical axis is logarithmic.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median contig N50 of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of QUAST.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Assembled length (bp)
    y_title: Contig N50 (bp)
    log_y: true
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: total_length
    y: n50
    label: assembly_id
    color: assembler
    size: n_contigs

- component: figure
  title: Assembled length per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is one assembly, with its total assembled length in base pairs, coloured by assembler. It answers how much of the community each assembler managed to assemble.
    How to read: a short bar next to its siblings on the same sample means that assembler lost sequence, often the low-coverage organisms. Read it beside the N50 plot, since a long assembly in fragments is still hard to bin.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median assembled length of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of QUAST.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: assembly_id
    y: total_length
    color: assembler
    labels:
      assembly_id: Assembly
      total_length: Assembled length (bp)
      assembler: Assembler
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: total_length

- component: figure
  title: Contig N50 by assembler
  description: |-
    Each bar is the contig N50 of one assembly, grouped by assembler and coloured by sample. It answers which assembler produces the longest contigs.
    How to read: N50 is the contig length such that contigs of at least that length cover half of the assembly, so a higher bar means a more contiguous assembly. An assembler that wins on every sample is the safer choice for binning.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median contig N50 of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of QUAST.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: assembler
    y: n50
    color: sample
    barmode: group
    labels:
      assembler: Assembler
      n50: Contig N50 (bp)
      sample: Sample
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: n50

- component: card
  title: Assembled length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the summed length of every assembly in view, and the bar splits it by assembler. It answers how much sequence each assembler contributes.
    How to read: a sum mixes samples, so use the median and the maximum beside it for a per-assembly reading. An assembler with a thin segment recovered less of the community.
  column: total_length
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: assembler
  caption: assembled length, split by assembler

- component: card
  title: Contig N50
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median contig N50 over the assemblies in view, and the bars rank the assemblers by their median. It answers which assembler is the most contiguous.
    How to read: N50 is the contig length such that contigs of at least that length cover half of the assembly, so higher is better. Contig lengths span orders of magnitude, so the card ranks medians instead of drawing a box.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  column: n50
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: assembler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: median N50, by assembler

- component: card
  title: Contigs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of contigs over the assemblies in view, and the bars rank the assemblers by the contigs they produce. It answers which assembler fragments the community most.
    How to read: a much higher count for one assembler on the same samples means a more fragmented assembly, usually with a lower N50. Contigs under 500 bp are not counted by QUAST by default.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  column: n_contigs
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: assembler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: contigs, by assembler

- component: card
  title: Longest contig
  description: |-
    The hero number is the longest contig of any assembly in view, and the bars rank the assemblers by their longest contig. It answers whether any assembler reached genome-scale contigs.
    How to read: a very long contig means part of the community assembled in one piece. A low maximum next to a high total length points to a fragmented assembly.
  column: largest_contig
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: assembler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: longest contig, by assembler

- component: card
  title: GC content
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median GC percentage of the assemblies in view, and the box shows the spread across assemblies. It answers whether assemblers agree on the base composition of the community.
    How to read: assemblies of the same sample should give a similar GC. A shift points to one assembler recovering a different part of the community.
  column: gc_percent
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median GC, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Assembly statistics
  description: |-
    Each row is one assembly, with its contig counts, N50, N75, L50, L75, GC, unknown bases, predicted rRNA genes and the length held by contigs over 1 kbp. It answers the exact figures behind every tile.
    How to read: sort by N50 or total length to rank assemblies, or filter by assembler to compare them on one sample.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: bin_n50_vs_length
  title: Bin contiguity against bin length
  description: |-
    Each point is a recovered bin: its total length on the horizontal axis and the N50 of its contigs on the vertical axis, coloured by binner and sized by the number of contigs. It answers which bins are a few long contigs and which are a pile of fragments.
    How to read: bins toward the top are close to a single contiguous genome. Large points low on the axis hold many small contigs, so a high completeness estimate for them may be carried by fragments. Compare binners on the same assembly.
    Note: QUAST defines no pass mark for N50 or bin length. The vertical axis is logarithmic.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median contig N50 of the bins of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of QUAST.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Bin length (bp)
    y_title: Contig N50 of the bin (bp)
    log_y: true
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: total_length
    y: n50
    label: bin_id
    color: binner
    size: n_contigs

- component: advanced_viz
  id: bin_gc_vs_length
  title: Bin GC content against length
  description: |-
    Each point is a recovered bin: its total length and its GC percentage, coloured by the assembler it came from and sized by the number of contigs. It answers whether bins have a coherent base composition.
    How to read: bins of one organism sit at a single GC. A bin far from its neighbours, or one that is much longer than the rest, may mix several organisms, so check it against a completeness and contamination estimate.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Bin length (bp)
    y_title: GC content (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: total_length
    y: gc_percent
    label: bin_id
    color: assembler
    size: n_contigs

- component: figure
  title: Contigs per bin by binner
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the bins that hold a given number of contigs, coloured by binner. It answers how fragmented the recovered bins are.
    How to read: a distribution piled at low counts means bins close to whole genomes. A long tail of bins with hundreds of contigs is fragmented, and the binner that produces more of them is the weaker choice for this assembly.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of contigs per bin of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of QUAST.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: n_contigs
    color: binner
    labels:
      n_contigs: Contigs in the bin
      binner: Binner
      count: Bins
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: n_contigs

- component: card
  title: Bin length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median length of a recovered bin, and the box shows the spread across bins. It answers how large a typical bin is.
    How to read: compare bins of the same sample and binner. A bin much shorter than its siblings may be a partial genome, so read it with the contig counts.
  column: total_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median bin length, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Bin contig N50
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median contig N50 of the bins in view, and the bars rank the binners by their median. It answers which binner recovers the most contiguous bins.
    How to read: N50 is the contig length such that contigs of at least that length cover half of the bin, so higher is better. Values span orders of magnitude, so the card ranks medians instead of drawing a box.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  column: n50
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: binner
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: median N50, by binner

- component: card
  title: Contigs per bin
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of contigs in a bin, and the bars rank the assemblers by the median of their bins. It answers which assembler gives the least fragmented bins.
    How to read: a low median means bins close to whole genomes. A high median means bins assembled from many fragments, whichever binner grouped them.
  column: n_contigs
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: assembler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: median contigs per bin, by assembler

- component: card
  title: Recovered bins
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct bins, and the bars rank the binners by how many each recovered. It answers how productive each binner was.
    How to read: more bins is not better by itself, since fragmented or contaminated bins also count. Read it with the N50 and completeness tiles.
  column: bin_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: binner
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: bins, by binner

- component: card
  title: Bin GC content
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median GC percentage of the bins in view, and the histogram shows how bins distribute over GC. It answers how varied the community's base composition is.
    How to read: a broad, multi-peaked histogram is a diverse community. A single narrow peak points to few organisms or to a few dominant ones.
  column: gc_percent
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: bins, by GC content

- component: table
  title: Bin assembly statistics
  description: |-
    Each row is one recovered bin, with its sample, assembler, binner, contig counts, length, N50, GC and predicted rRNA genes. It answers the exact figures behind every tile.
    How to read: sort by N50 or contig count to find the best and the most fragmented bins, or filter by binner to compare them.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cumulative_length
  title: Assembled length kept at each minimum contig length
  description: |-
    Each curve is one assembly: the total length held by contigs of at least a given size, read at each minimum contig length QUAST reports. It answers how much of the assembly sits in long contigs.
    How to read: a curve that stays high toward the right keeps most of its sequence in long contigs, which a binner can work with. A curve that falls steeply between the first rungs holds its length in short fragments.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Minimum contig length (bp)
    y_title: Length held by contigs of at least that size (bp)
  roles:
    series: assembly_id
    x: min_contig_length
    y: total_length

- component: advanced_viz
  id: retained_fraction
  title: Share of the assembly kept at each minimum contig length
  description: |-
    Each curve is one assembly: the share of its total length held by contigs of at least a given size. It answers how quickly an assembly loses sequence as short contigs are set aside, independent of its size.
    How to read: curves that stay near 1 are dominated by long contigs. Curves that collapse early are drifts of short fragments that will bin into chimeras, so compare assemblies on the same sample.
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Minimum contig length (bp)
    y_title: Share of the assembled length
  roles:
    series: assembly_id
    x: min_contig_length
    y: length_fraction

- component: figure
  title: Contigs surviving each minimum length
  description: |-
    Each line is one assembly: the number of contigs of at least a given size at each minimum length QUAST reports. It answers how many contigs a size filter leaves.
    How to read: a line that drops by orders of magnitude after the first rung is mostly short contigs. A flat line is an assembly of a few long contigs. The vertical axis is logarithmic.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: min_contig_length
    y: n_contigs
    color: assembly_id
    log_y: true
    labels:
      min_contig_length: Minimum contig length (bp)
      n_contigs: Contigs
      assembly_id: Assembly

- component: card
  title: Length in contigs of 5 kbp or more
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of an assembly held by contigs of at least 5 kbp, and the box shows the spread across assemblies. It answers how much of a typical assembly is in contigs long enough to bin.
    How to read: a share near 1 means most of the sequence is in long contigs. A low share means a fragmented assembly, so open the curves to see where it falls.
    Note: 5 kbp is one rung QUAST reports, chosen to read one point of the curve, not a published cut-off.
  column: length_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('min_contig_length') == 5000
  caption: median share, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Contigs before any size filter
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest contig count of any assembly in view, and the bars rank the assemblers by their largest count. It answers which assembler produces the most fragments.
    How to read: a high count means a fragmented assembly. Read it beside the retained-length curves to see how much sequence those contigs hold.
  column: n_contigs
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: assembler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: most contigs, by assembler

- component: table
  title: Contig length ladder
  description: |-
    Each row is one assembly at one minimum contig length, with the contig count, the total length and the share of the assembly held. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: filter to one assembly to read its ladder rung by rung.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: fraction_vs_misassemblies
  title: Reference covered against misassemblies
  description: |-
    Each point is one assembly aligned to the reference: the share of the reference it covers on the horizontal axis and the number of misassemblies on the vertical axis, sized by NGA50. It answers which assemblies cover the reference without breaking it.
    How to read: points toward the lower right cover most of the reference with few joins the reference does not support. A high point has a long N50 bought with misassemblies, so read it beside NGA50.
    Note: QUAST defines no pass mark for genome fraction or misassemblies.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of misassemblies of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of QUAST.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Genome fraction (% of the reference covered)
    y_title: Misassemblies
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: genome_fraction
    y: misassemblies
    label: assembly_id
    color: report_id
    size: nga50

- component: figure
  title: NGA50 per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is one assembly: its NGA50, the contiguity left once the assembly is cut at every misassembly and unaligned region, shaded by the genome fraction it covers. It answers how contiguous each assembly is against the reference.
    How to read: NGA50 is the length of a block such that blocks of at least that length cover half of the reference. A bar much shorter than the assembly's N50 means contiguity bought with joins the reference does not support.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median NGA50 of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of QUAST.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: report_id
    y: nga50
    color: genome_fraction
    labels:
      report_id: Assembly
      nga50: NGA50 (bp)
      genome_fraction: Genome fraction (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: nga50

- component: card
  title: Reference covered
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of the reference covered by an assembly, and the box shows the spread across assemblies. It answers how complete the assemblies are against the reference.
    How to read: a value near 100 means the reference is almost fully assembled. A low value means missing regions, or a reference that differs from the sample.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  column: genome_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median coverage, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Misassemblies
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of misassemblies over the assemblies in view, and the box shows how they spread per assembly. It answers how often the assemblies disagree with the reference.
    How to read: fewer is better, and a few assemblies carrying most of them point to an assembler or a setting to revisit. Compare with N50 and NGA50 before trusting a long assembly.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  column: misassemblies
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: misassemblies per assembly, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Mismatches per 100 kbp
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of mismatches per 100 kbp of aligned sequence, and the box shows the spread across assemblies. It answers how accurate the assembled bases are.
    How to read: lower is better. A high rate points to a polishing or error-correction problem, or to a reference that differs from the sample.
    Source: https://github.com/ablab/quast/blob/master/README.md
  column: mismatches_per_100kbp
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median rate, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Assembly against the reference
  description: |-
    Each row is one assembly aligned to the reference, with its genome fraction, duplication ratio, misassemblies, mismatch and indel rates, NG50 and NGA50. It answers the exact figures behind every tile.
    How to read: sort by NGA50 to rank assemblies, then check their misassemblies and duplication ratio.
